post.description:
Mint the money-plane token pair for an already-identified user, keyed by their
 concierge user id. Service-to-service: authenticated by the shared issuance token
 in the `authorization` metadata (Bearer), never a user token. The user must already
 exist locally (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and not be frozen.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evbanking_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected hub-side.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).

Dispatch a queued withdrawal to custody once its rail has liquidity (the treasury
 worker). Stands in for an automated rebalance/top-up trigger. Idempotent.

Fail a processing user withdrawal that never reached the chain: voids the
 reservation, refunding the user. NEVER call this if the broadcast may have landed
 on-chain — that would double-pay. Idempotent.
Operator (TreasuryRead): the money-plane operations mode (the read-only kill-switch).

The treasury: per-rail on-chain liquidity (Layer 2) and the claims it backs
 (Layer 1), read live from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
Operator (TreasuryRead): outbox rows the relay parked (needs-intervention).

Operator (TreasuryRead): every rail, whether this deployment runs it, and whether an
 operator froze it.

Admin (WithdrawalSettle): the cross-user queue of withdrawals awaiting operator
 action, oldest first — `queued` (awaiting liquidity/dispatch) and `processing`
 (broadcast in flight: settle with the mined tx ref, or fail ONLY if nothing
 reached the chain). The admin Withdrawals screen's clear-the-queue surface.

post.summary:
Admin (DepositAddressMigrate): retire a user's HEALTHY, KEK-sealed deposit address
 in favour of one minted inside the key custodian's enclave (phase 4 of
 docs/MIGRATION-turnkey.md), and refresh the hub's address cache.
post.description:
NOT the rotation path. Rotation recovers a key that is already dead; this retires a
 live one, so the hub must first prove the address has nothing left on it — refused
 while the user has any credited deposit on this rail that no sweep has observed
 drained. The signer independently refuses a dead key, an already-migrated row, and
 an address other than the one this hub cleared.

Record a settled on-chain deposit, crediting a party's claim. Idempotent by
 `tx_ref` — recording the same chain tx twice credits once.

Admin (DepositAddressRotate): supersede a user's PROVABLY DEAD deposit address
 (the signer can no longer unseal its key — the KEK-epoch casualty class) with a
 freshly minted keypair, and refresh the hub's address cache. The signer refuses
 to rotate a key that still unseals. Funds already on the old address remain
 unrecoverable; this restores the user's ability to receive FUTURE deposits.

Admin (OperationsManage): toggle read-only mode. When on, every user money mutation
 (withdraw, payment, compartment move, invoice payment) is rejected — "pause deposits & withdrawals".

Admin (OperationsManage): freeze/unfreeze a rail — no new deposit addresses or
 withdrawals on it, queued withdrawals held, and no treasury gas alert.

Settle a user withdrawal once it has the required on-chain confirmations: posts the
 reservation and moves the net out of custody. `tx_ref` is the chain transaction.
 Stands in for a chain watcher + custody confirmation callback. Idempotent.

Admin (OutboxManage): clear `parked_at` so the relay re-drives the event once the
 cause is fixed; refused for a compensated row — it parked half-applied with
 compensation owed, so re-driving would re-apply the legs that already posted.

The caller's balance in ONE scope (`main` included), for a client that shows a single
 compartment and must not read the sum over all of them. An unknown scope is NOT_FOUND.

A scope service's stored request for a mandate (`scope.v1.MandateRequestService`),
 for the caller to read before granting it. Unknown, expired and malformed ids are
 the same NOT_FOUND; the id is a lowercase uuid.

One scope's policy, read-only. The platform owners set it (an approval of kind
 `bank:compartment_policy`), never the user.

Let a scope's service draw on the caller's compartment in that scope — hold it
 (a subscription, a buy order) or charge it — within the caps of the service's
 request, which the caller grants as it stands (`request_id`; unknown or expired is
 NOT_FOUND). This is
 the only consent a service's debit stands on; without it the service can only
 send an invoice. A client that banking's grants do not allow to touch users'
 compartments in the scope is INVALID_ARGUMENT. One live mandate per (scope,
 client): granting again replaces it — new holds and charges draw on the new one,
 while holds already standing stay under the mandate they were placed with until they
 finish. The new mandate still binds them: none outlives its `expires_at`, and a
 capture of one into another user needs BOOK_FILL from both. Naturally confirmed on
 the caller's first move into the scope, on one screen.

Every scope the caller could hold money in: `main` first, then each scope banking
 knows, with the caller's balance there (zero if never entered) and its policy.

The caller's live mandates, and replaced ones whose holds still hold money, newest
 first.

Move money between `main` and one scope compartment — exactly one side is `main`.
 Moving IN is checked against the scope's policy: FAILED_PRECONDITION with the
 failed rule (`kyc_level`, `max_per_move`, `max_moved_in_24h`, `max_balance`) when
 it does not pass. Moving OUT is never limited by policy, only by what is available
 in the compartment. Either way `insufficient_funds` when the source, less the
 caller's moves still in flight, cannot cover it; the limits count moves in flight too.
 A key reused with different terms is ALREADY_EXISTS. The move is recorded at once and
 posted to the ledger by the hub: the result's `state` is `pending` until then,
 `posted` after, or `failed` (with `failure_reason`) if the ledger refused it or the
 hub could not post it — a failed move is final and is never carried out later.

End a live mandate at once. Every hold the client still has on the caller's
 compartment in the scope is voided — under this mandate or one it replaced — so the
 money is back with the caller, and the service learns it from the money events. A
 mandate already revoked or replaced is returned as it is; anyone else's, or an
 unknown id, is NOT_FOUND.

The invoice as the payer sees it. Unknown ids and invoices restricted to another
 payer are the SAME NOT_FOUND.

Pay an OPEN invoice. FAILED_PRECONDITION when it is no longer open, when the
 chosen source cannot cover it, or when the payer is below the receiving scope's
 `min_kyc_level`. A repeat with the same `idempotency_key` returns
 the invoice you paid; paying it again under a new key is FAILED_PRECONDITION.
 PAID MEANS POSTED. The answer is the invoice as it stands now: `processing` while the
 ledger has not taken the payment (normally milliseconds), `paid` once it has. A
 payment the ledger refuses puts the invoice back to `open`, payable again. Poll
 `GetPayableInvoice` until it leaves `processing`.
The caller's operations, newest first, across every kind.

Answer: APPROVE or REJECT. Idempotent for the same answer; a different one after an
 answer is ALREADY_EXISTS. An approval is gated like any money the caller moves (revoked
 tokens, the operator's pause, a frozen account) and executed at once; a failure in the
 execution is the order's to record and does not undo the answer. A seat whose pins have
 moved (the caller's sessions were revoked, or their mailbox changed, since the order
 opened) fails the order closed and answers ALREADY_EXISTS with the reason.
One order as its subject may see it, whatever state it is in.
The caller's orders waiting for their answer, newest first.
Withdraw an order the CALLER opened, while it is still pending. Anyone else is refused.
One order in full (Admin/Owner).
The payment history, newest first, filtered (Admin/Owner). Nothing is ever deleted.

Open a payment order (Admin/Owner). Refused when the source cannot cover the amount
 right now, when the shape could never execute (an unconfigured rail, a sub-minimum
 external amount, the treasury as a destination), or when the source is the treasury
 (closed, D24).

The id of the concierge approval opened for a payout operation, so the BFF can ask
 concierge whether the caller is on its roster BEFORE any recipient is read. Carries no
 line, no amount and no name.

One page of the operation's lines, with the summary every page repeats. `approval_id`
 must be the operation's own (from GetPayoutApproval).

Admin (allowlist): disable a user, freezing future sign-in/refresh without
 deleting the record.

The calling user's live balance — `main` plus their scope compartments — read straight
 from TigerBeetle (Read-First).
 No Postgres-stored amount exists; the response is authoritative as of `as_of`.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserBalanceRead): read ANY user's live balance by id — the operator
 console's user-detail drawer. The self-service GetBalance above acts on the
 caller's own `sub`; this one takes an explicit target and is role-gated.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected hub-side. The token-revocation control surface.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

Cancel one of the caller's still-queued withdrawals (refund). Rejected once the
 withdrawal is processing (a broadcast may have landed).
The caller's deposit address on a network (stable; derived once and reused).

The caller's wallet — the unified lifecycle balance, deposit addresses, and the
 per-rail withdrawable view.
The caller's confirmed on-chain deposits, newest first.
The caller's withdrawals, newest first.

Request an on-chain withdrawal of free balance to an external address. Accepted
 (and reserved) as long as the unified balance covers it; it ships immediately when
 the chosen rail is liquid, otherwise it is queued until the treasury tops it up.

post.summary:
Redeem a one-time authorization code for a RELYING PARTY's own token pair — the
 back half of the code flow a first-party client on another origin (the Service-Arb
 panel) runs against `GET /auth/authorize` (publicly `evinvest.ltd/api/auth/authorize`).
 Called server-to-server by the client's backend, authenticated by its client
 secret. The code is single-use, lives 60s, and is bound to the client, the exact
 redirect_uri and the PKCE (S256) challenge sent to authorize; presenting a code
 twice is refused AND revokes every token issued off it.
post.description:
The access token is `typ=access` with `aud=<the client's audience>` (e.g. `sa`) and
 a TTL of at most 15 minutes. It opens exactly one RPC in this plane —
 `UserDirectory.GetMe`, which answers it with a trimmed profile (no identity-document
 fields, no KYC level) — and is refused (UNAUTHENTICATED) everywhere else, here and
 on the money plane. Signing out of evinvest.ltd (Logout, RevokeSession, revoke-all)
 revokes the client sessions that sign-in authorized. The refresh token is opaque and bound to the client.
 The access token carries `auth_time` ONLY when the code ended a confirmation that
 this authorization asked for (`max_age`, docs/SCOPES-AND-APPROVALS.md §3.2): the unix
 seconds of the evinvest.ltd session's re-authentication. Any other code gives tokens
 without it. That is how a client proves a fresh confirmation to
 ApprovalExecutionService.Propose.

Publish the current signing public keys (JWKS). Polled by downstream services'
 `evconcierge_auth` verifier to refresh its local cache; also consulted on an
 unknown-`kid` miss. Carries only public key material.

List the caller's active sessions (refresh-token families). Identity is proven by
 the presented refresh token (the BFF holds it server-side); the family that owns
 that token is flagged `current`.

Revoke the presented refresh token's family. With `revoke_all` set, also bumps
 the user's `token_version` so every outstanding access token is rejected.

A relying party publishes its tenant's catalog: the permissions and aliases its
 namespace defines. Authenticated by the client secret, like ExchangeCode. Refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT) when anything lies outside the tenant's namespace, an alias names
 a permission the catalog does not define, a delegated alias delegates in turn, the
 catalog exceeds 1024 permissions or 128 aliases or a name exceeds 128 characters, or
 `version` lies more than a day ahead of this plane's clock; FAILED_PRECONDITION when
 `version` is older than the stored one, or equal with different content. Every
 published catalog is kept. Grants whose target the new catalog drops stay, grant
 nothing, and are listed as orphaned.

Rotate a refresh token: returns a fresh access+refresh pair and invalidates
 the presented refresh token (rotation + reuse detection in the central store).

Rotate a relying party's refresh token. The account is re-checked on EVERY rotation,
 so a suspension ends the session at the next refresh rather than at the family's
 deadline; presenting a rotated-out token revokes the family. The new access token
 keeps the session's original `auth_time`: a refresh never moves it.

Revoke one of the caller's sessions by id (must belong to the same user). Revoking
 the current session is allowed (acts like a sign-out of this device).

post.summary:
DEPRECATED — always refuses, naming HoldUser or
 ApprovalService.ProposeUserSuspension.
post.description:
The verb was ambiguous in the one way that mattered: it was both the emergency
 brake (the frozen flag the money plane re-reads at dispatch, which stops a
 withdrawal already in the queue) and a permanent judgement on an account, decided
 by one person with no record of why. Those need opposite treatments — the first
 must stay instant, the second must not be one person's to make — so the caller now
 has to say which one they mean. Kept in the contract rather than deleted so an
 older console gets an explanatory refusal instead of an UNIMPLEMENTED.
The calling user's own identity (resolved from the access-token `sub`).

Admin (UserRead): the full profile of ANY user by id (the admin sibling of the
 self-only GetMe), for the user-detail drawer.

post.summary:
Grant a user a target inside a tenant's namespace: an alias (`sa:operator`), a
 permission (`sa:work:leads:read`) or a `*` pattern (`sa:work:*`). Nothing grants
 anything in the `iam`, `concierge`, `bank` or `seat` namespaces (INVALID_ARGUMENT),
 and nobody grants to their own account (PERMISSION_DENIED). A target the tenant's
 catalog does not define grants nothing and is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Re-granting what is
 held is a no-op.
post.description:
Who may: a seat holding `iam:tenants:grant` — any target. The holder of an alias the
 catalog lets delegate (`delegations`) — exactly the aliases it delegates, naming the
 user by `account` (an email or a username) only (a `user_id` is PERMISSION_DENIED:
 ids are visible in the roster, and granting one would reveal its owner's address).
 Anyone else, or a target outside the delegation: PERMISSION_DENIED, before the user
 is looked up. An email names the accounts it is verified on or backs a password of;
 only when it names none is the handle read as a username.

 To a seat: an unknown user or handle is NOT_FOUND; a handle naming several
 accounts, or a disabled/held account, is FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason. To a
 delegate all three are the SAME FAILED_PRECONDITION ("this address cannot be granted
 access"), so a grant never tells them whether, or how, a handle is known. A
 delegate gets a budget of GrantPermission + RevokePermission calls per hour
 (refusals included); past it, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.

Admin (UserSuspend): the emergency brake. Freezes the account NOW and lapses on
 its own after 24h unless the owners ratify it with ProposeUserSuspension. One actor
 may stop money temporarily; one actor may never stop it permanently. Emits
 SUSPENDED across the cross-plane bridge, and REINSTATED again when it lapses.

The active grants inside one tenant namespace, with each holder's identity. A seat
 holding `iam:tenants:grant`, or a delegate of that namespace — who gets `legal_name`
 AND `preferred_name` empty: the team sees each other's email, username and grant, and
 nothing that says who an address belongs to.

Admin (UserRead): list/search users for the operator console — paginated, with a
 free-text query and optional role/status filters (see ListUsersRequest). Returns
 lightweight summaries, not full profiles.

post.summary:
Admin (allowlist): re-enable a disabled user, lifting the sign-in/refresh
 freeze. Emits REINSTATED across the cross-plane bridge.
post.description:
Refuses with FAILED_PRECONDITION when the suspension was the owners' verdict,
 naming ApprovalService.ProposeUserReinstatement — otherwise one admin could
 overturn a consilium and the consilium would be advisory.

Take a grant away. Same authority as GrantPermission, either addressing form for a
 delegate too: the answer depends only on a grant they can already list. NOT_FOUND when
 the user holds no active grant of that target — including a handle naming nobody, or
 several accounts. Shares GrantPermission's budget.

Admin (allowlist): bump a user's token_version so all their outstanding access
 tokens are rejected. The token-revocation control surface.

post.summary:
Admin (allowlist): set a user's KYC level. Emits KYC_CHANGED across the
 cross-plane bridge (so the money plane learns the new level). Echoes the
 level now in effect.
post.description:
Refuses with PERMISSION_DENIED when user_id is the CALLER's own account.
 KycManage is held by Admin as well as Owner, and tier 1 is the floor for
 withdrawals on the money plane, so without this an operator could lift their
 own money gate. A console must not offer this control on the operator's own
 row: the refusal is decided from the session alone and belongs in front of
 the call. Raising your own level goes through the verification front door,
 which reaches tier 1; above that, and for any downgrade, another holder of
 KycManage acts.

Admin (RoleGrant, Owner only): set a user's platform access role. Emits
 ROLE_CHANGED across the cross-plane bridge so the money plane mirrors it. Echoes
 the role now in effect.

Update the caller's own editable profile fields (full-replace of the set in
 UpdateProfileRequest). Identity/auth fields (email, status) are not editable here.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description:
The target: the CONCIERGE user id (the handle the operator console carries from
 the identity plane's ListUsers) or the banking user id. Resolution is
 concierge-first via the bridge mirror (`users.concierge_user_id`), falling back
 to the banking id (existing money-plane callers stay valid); an id matching
 neither returns NOT_FOUND — never an authoritative zero.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: APPROVE or REJECT. PENDING is rejected as an invalid argument.

client_ip.title: client_ip
client_ip.description: Audit only — the edge supplies these; they are never trusted for authorization.

client_ip.title: client_ip
client_ip.description: browser address as seen by the trusted proxy hop

user_agent.title: user_agent
user_agent.description: clamped to 256 bytes by the hub

intent_id.title: intent_id
intent_id.description: the wallet intent this act executes (empty before intents exist)

banking.v1.AuditContext.title: AuditContext
banking.v1.AuditContext.description:
Who asked, and from where, for an act that moves or authorises money. Filled by the BFF
 (never by a browser): recorded beside the act for the audit trail and, for `origin`, the
 input to the limit profile (a first-party origin or a scope host). `client_ip` is the
 address the trusted proxy hop saw, not a caller-supplied header. Every field may be empty
 (a caller that predates the message): the act is audited blank and, for a withdrawal, judged
 on the tighter host profile — a missing origin fails closed.

in_compartments.title: in_compartments
in_compartments.description: the caller's money in scope compartments (CompartmentService), still theirs

banking.v1.Balance.title: Balance
banking.v1.Balance.description:
The user's single, network-agnostic balance, segmented by lifecycle. Every figure is
 a TigerBeetle-authoritative decimal USDT string; total = available + pending_withdrawal
 + in_compartments.

banking.v1.ClaimBalance.title: ClaimBalance
banking.v1.ClaimBalance.description:
A claim's cash, split the way every reader needs it and read off ONE ledger balance, so
 the three can never disagree: `posted` is settled, `reserved` is spoken for by approved
 payments out of it that have not settled, and `available = posted − reserved` is what a
 new payment may take.

display_name.title: display_name
display_name.description: the scope's human name, as concierge announced it

available.title: available
available.description: free to spend in the scope or move back to main

held.title: held
held.description: held by the scope's services (resting orders, pending subscriptions)

banking.v1.Compartment.title: Compartment
banking.v1.Compartment.description: One compartment of the caller. Decimal USDT strings; total = available + held.

failure_reason.title: failure_reason
failure_reason.description: set only when `failed`: `insufficient_funds`, or `parked:<kind>` when the hub could not post it

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the credit

banking.v1.Deposit.title: Deposit
banking.v1.Deposit.description: A confirmed on-chain deposit credited to the caller's unified balance.

min_confirmations.title: min_confirmations
min_confirmations.description: confirmations before a deposit is credited

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether this rail is on testnet — the client uses it to render the correct address
 form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged user-friendly address). Only meaningful per rail; false
 for a mainnet rail.

banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.title: DepositScanCursor
banking.v1.DepositScanCursor.description:
Seconds since a rail's deposit watcher last advanced/touched its per-network scan
 cursor (refreshed only by a completed scan cycle, so age ≈ time since the last
 healthy cycle; thresholds are the consumer's concern).

network.title: network
network.description: Rail the payment ships on (BEP20 / POLYGON / TRC20 / TON).

address.title: address
address.description: Destination address, rendered in FULL wherever a human approves it.

operation_id.title: operation_id
operation_id.description: The operation id: a lowercase UUID, the tail of the approval's `pending_operation:<id>`.

request_id.title: request_id
request_id.description: a lowercase uuid, from the service's grant link

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description: 1..128 chars; a repeat returns the original mandate

banking.v1.GrantMandateRequest.title: GrantMandateRequest
banking.v1.GrantMandateRequest.description:
The caps are decimal USDT. What counts against them is the client's draws on the caller's
 compartment in the scope — under this mandate and any it replaced, so granting again
 never resets a cap: a hold counts at its full amount from when it is placed, until it is
 voided or expires, when only what was captured of it still counts; a capture of a hold
 placed more than 24 h ago counts from when it is made.

concierge_user_id.title: concierge_user_id
concierge_user_id.description:
The concierge canonical user id (a UUID) of the already-authenticated user. Banking
 maps it to its local mirror row (provisioned by the cross-plane bridge) and mints the
 money-plane pair for that user. Banking never sees Google's `sub` — the bridge carries
 it; the BFF carries this concierge id, which it has from the concierge sign-in.

user_agent.title: user_agent
user_agent.description:
Device metadata captured by the BFF at sign-in, stored on the refresh-token family
 for the "sessions & devices" surface. Best-effort, free-form.

banking.v1.Jwk.title: Jwk
banking.v1.Jwk.description:
One JSON Web Key. Ed25519 keys are OKP: kty="OKP", crv="Ed25519", x=base64url
 public key, alg="EdDSA". `kid` is a stable thumbprint of the public key.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Rows to return. 0 means the server default (100); the server caps it at 200.

party.title: party
party.description: Either end. Unset means every party.

treasury_only.title: treasury_only
treasury_only.description: Only orders whose source is banking's treasury — the ones the owners gate.

offset.title: offset
offset.description: Lines to skip, in the order they are paid. Past the end is an empty page.

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Lines to return. 0 means the server default (50); the server caps it at 200.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token: proves identity and flags the current session.

revoke_all.title: revoke_all
revoke_all.description:
When true, bump the user's token_version (coarse "revoke all"), not just this
 refresh family.

used_24h.title: used_24h
used_24h.description: drawn in the rolling 24 h, decimal USDT

outstanding.title: outstanding
outstanding.description: held by the client's active holds now

book_filled_24h.title: book_filled_24h
book_filled_24h.description: sent to other users in the rolling 24 h

replaced_at.title: replaced_at
replaced_at.description: 0 unless a later grant replaced it; then `outstanding` is its own holds'

banking.v1.MandateOperation.title: MandateOperation
banking.v1.MandateOperation.description: What a mandate lets the service do with the caller's compartment.

expires_at.title: expires_at
expires_at.description: unix seconds: until when this request can be granted

banking.v1.MandateRequest.title: MandateRequest
banking.v1.MandateRequest.description: What a service asks the caller to grant, as banking stored it. Amounts are decimal USDT.

old_address.title: old_address
old_address.description: the retired address — kept so the operator can watch it

new_address.title: new_address
new_address.description: the NEW fundable, custody-held deposit address

to_scope.title: to_scope
to_scope.description: the other side; one of the two must be `main`

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description: client-minted (a UUID per click); a repeat returns the original move

withdrawable.title: withdrawable
withdrawable.description: max requestable on this rail (= available)

withdrawal_fee.title: withdrawal_fee
withdrawal_fee.description: flat network fee retained on a withdrawal

banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.title: NetworkWithdrawable
banking.v1.NetworkWithdrawable.description:
Per-rail withdrawal options (the accept-and-queue UX). `withdrawable` is the whole
 available balance (a request beyond `instant` is accepted and queued); `instant` is
 the portion that ships without queueing = min(available, rail liquidity).

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Required. Bounded at 500 bytes, no control characters; it is INSIDE the hashed
 payload the approver signs.

id.title: id
id.description:
Unique within the feed: the aggregate UUID for a withdrawal, the on-chain `tx_ref`
 for a deposit (which has no surrogate id).

state.title: state
state.description:
Lifecycle, per kind. deposit: always `credited` (the row exists only once the
 watcher has confirmed it). withdrawal: queued | processing | completed | failed |
 cancelled.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: unix seconds the hub recorded the operation

amount.title: amount
amount.description: Cash moved, as a magnitude — the sign is implied by `kind`, never encoded here.

net_amount.title: net_amount
net_amount.description: withdrawal only — amount − fee, what ships on-chain

scope.title: scope
scope.description:
The wallet compartment the row belongs to: `main` for every kind this feed carries
 (deposits and withdrawals are main's). A client in scope mode keeps only the rows
 whose `scope` is its own; compartment moves and scope payouts are not in this feed.

banking.v1.Operation.title: Operation
banking.v1.Operation.description:
One row of the timeline. `kind` is the discriminator — it decides which of the
 remaining fields carry a value; the rest are empty. Deliberately flat rather than a
 oneof: the whole surface is projected to TypeScript through OpenAPI, where a flat
 message with a documented discriminator survives the pipeline unambiguously.

 | field        | deposit | withdrawal |
 | ------------ | ------- | ---------- |
 | amount       | ✓       | ✓ (gross)  |
 | fee          |         | ✓          |
 | net_amount   |         | ✓          |
 | network      | ✓       | ✓          |
 | address      |         | ✓          |
 | tx_ref       | ✓       | ✓ at settle|

truncated.title: truncated
truncated.description:
True when the caller's history is longer than `limit` — the client is looking at
 the newest page, not the whole record.

banking.v1.ParkedEvent.title: ParkedEvent
banking.v1.ParkedEvent.description:
One parked outbox row. `reason` is the relay's last error; `parked_at` is unix
 seconds; `compensated` marks a half-applied event that is owed compensation
 (never unparkable).

kind.title: kind
kind.description:
user | treasury. `treasury` is banking's own (D17), never a destination, and closed as
 a source until concierge's scope approvals decide its spending (D24); its id is empty
 or `main:treasury`.

id.title: id
id.description:
For `user`, the CONCIERGE user id the console carries (resolved to the money-plane id here; a banking id is
 accepted as a fallback, the way UsersService.GetUserBalance resolves one).

banking.v1.Party.title: Party
banking.v1.Party.description: One end of a payment, as a REQUEST names it.

pay_from.title: pay_from
pay_from.description: `main`, or the invoice's scope (the caller's compartment there)

state.title: state
state.description:
open | processing | paid | cancelled | expired. `paid` only once the ledger has posted
 the payment; `processing` until then (it ends as `paid`, or back at `open` if refused).

paid_at.title: paid_at
paid_at.description: unix seconds, once paid (posted), to the payer only

available_main.title: available_main
available_main.description:
What the caller could pay from right now, decimal USDT: their `main` available
 balance and their available balance in this scope's compartment.

tier.title: tier
tier.description: internal | external — DERIVED from the destination, never supplied.

amount.title: amount
amount.description: Decimal USDT string, as everywhere else on this wire.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Why, in the initiator's words. Required, shown verbatim, never interpreted.

requirement.title: requirement
requirement.description: owners_approval | subject_consent — the one requirement, read off the source.

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms, re-verified at execution.

executed_withdrawal_id.title: executed_withdrawal_id
executed_withdrawal_id.description:
Set on EXECUTED for an external order only: an internal one settled as a ledger
 transfer and records no id of its own.

seat.title: seat
seat.description:
The seat that decides the order: `concierge_approval` (a `bank:payment` approval) or
 `session` (the investor's answer in the wallet host).

approval_id.title: approval_id
approval_id.description: Concierge's id of the approval, once banking has opened it; set for `concierge_approval`.

session_decision.title: session_decision
session_decision.description: The investor's own answer, set for `session`.

payload_hash.title: payload_hash
payload_hash.description: Hex SHA-256 over the canonical terms the answer binds to.

decision.title: decision
decision.description: This seat's own answer; PENDING until they give one.

invalidated.title: invalidated
invalidated.description:
True when one of the pins recorded at open has moved: the order can no longer be
 answered or executed.

banking.v1.PaymentConfirmation.title: PaymentConfirmation
banking.v1.PaymentConfirmation.description:
One order as the investor it spends is shown it: the terms they answer and nothing about
 the operator beyond a masked address.

banking.v1.PaymentDestination.title: PaymentDestination
banking.v1.PaymentDestination.description:
Where a payment lands. An external SOURCE is unrepresentable on purpose: money cannot
 arrive from an address by anyone's say-so — that is a deposit, which a chain watcher
 attests.

kind.title: kind
kind.description: user | treasury, or `external` for an address.

id.title: id
id.description:
The MONEY-PLANE user id (the request accepts a concierge id; the
 response carries what the order stored). Empty for addresses.

detail.title: detail
detail.description:
What a person recognises this end BY, beside the label: the receiving investor's
 MASKED mailbox for `user`. Empty otherwise. Never
 part of the digest — the label is what an approval binds.

banking.v1.PaymentEnd.title: PaymentEnd
banking.v1.PaymentEnd.description:
One end of a payment, as a RESPONSE describes it. `label` is the wording every approval
 surface shares; the structured
 fields let a screen link to the account.

banking.v1.PaymentState.title: PaymentState
banking.v1.PaymentState.description: Where an order stands. Terminal everywhere except PENDING and APPROVED.

total.title: total
total.description: Canonical decimal USDT; the sum of ALL lines, not of this page.

max_line.title: max_line
max_line.description: The largest single line, as the approval shows it.

recipients.title: recipients
recipients.description: How many lines the payout has in all.

recipients_without_history.title: recipients_without_history
recipients_without_history.description: How many of them are recipients without history in the scope.

lines_digest.title: lines_digest
lines_digest.description:
SHA-256 over the lines, as stored with the operation. The hub recomputes it from the
 lines it reads and refuses the page when they differ.

offset.title: offset
offset.description: The page asked for, echoed so a client can tell which one it holds.

line_no.title: line_no
line_no.description: The place in the payout, from 0.

recipient.title: recipient
recipient.description: The recipient as the requesting service named them — the string `lines_digest` covers.

no_history.title: no_history
no_history.description:
The recipient has no earlier POSTED approved payout in this scope: banking has never
 paid them through an approval here, so an approver has nothing to compare the line with.
 Pending payouts do not count (they may still fail), nor do the service's automatic
 payouts (redemption, book, fee rebate) or this operation's own.

banking.v1.PayoutReviewLine.title: PayoutReviewLine
banking.v1.PayoutReviewLine.description: One recipient and what they are paid.

custody.title: custody
custody.description: liquid on-chain USDT held in this rail's custody wallet

treasury_address.title: treasury_address
treasury_address.description: the rail's hot wallet — fund USDT (liquidity) + gas here

onchain_usdt.title: onchain_usdt
onchain_usdt.description: decimal USDT actually on-chain in the treasury wallet

onchain_gas.title: onchain_gas
onchain_gas.description: decimal native units (BNB | TRX | TON) for gas

gas_station_address.title: gas_station_address
gas_station_address.description:
The rail's sweep GAS-STATION wallet — a separate account paying the gas drops
 that consolidate user deposits into the treasury. Fund the native coin here,
 never USDT. Empty when the rail has no gas-station view.

is_testnet.title: is_testnet
is_testnet.description:
Whether the addresses above are testnet-tagged, so a client can render them in the
 rail's user-facing form (e.g. TON's testnet-tagged friendly address). Only
 meaningful per rail; false where the rail's address form is network-agnostic.

banking.v1.RailLiquidity.title: RailLiquidity
banking.v1.RailLiquidity.description:
Per-rail on-chain liquidity (the treasury / Layer 2). The `treasury_*`/`onchain_*`
 fields are the operator funding view, read best-effort from the chain — empty means
 the rail is unconfigured or the read was unavailable, never an error.

scan_cursors.title: scan_cursors
scan_cursors.description:
Per-rail deposit-scan diagnostics; only configured rails appear. A large age on
 a configured rail means the deposit scan is stalled — deposits confirm on-chain
 but are not credited. Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

unseal_failures.title: unseal_failures
unseal_failures.description:
Signer unseal failures seen on money-moving paths (sweep / withdrawal signing)
 since this instance booted. Any non-zero value means a PROVABLY DEAD key (the
 KEK-epoch bug class) was asked to sign — funds on its address cannot move.
 Diagnostics only: it does NOT gate `ready`.

banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse
banking.v1.ReadinessResponse.description:
`ready` is the gate the orchestrator acts on; the rest are diagnostics so a
 not-ready response says *why* without scraping logs. `parked_rows` are outbox
 events the relay could not apply (need operator intervention); `backlog` is the
 count of undispatched rows and the age of the oldest, surfacing a wedged relay.

network.title: network
network.description: bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton — the rail it arrived on

expected_amount.title: expected_amount
expected_amount.description:
Optional operator assertion in decimal USDT. When set it must equal what the chain
 reports or the call is refused, so a mistyped reference fails loudly instead of
 silently crediting some other transfer.

banking.v1.RecordDepositRequest.title: RecordDepositRequest
banking.v1.RecordDepositRequest.description:
Record an arrival that reached a rail out of band, PROVEN against the chain.

 The caller supplies only a pointer to a fact: the reference is read back from the chain
 and the amount and the credited party are taken from what is actually there. An operator
 therefore cannot mint a balance by typing one — the worst a wrong reference can do is
 name a transfer that does not exist, or one that did not land on an address of ours,
 and both are rejected.

recorded.title: recorded
recorded.description: false if `tx_ref` was already recorded (idempotent no-op)

amount.title: amount
amount.description: what the CHAIN reported, decimal USDT — never the caller's number

banking.v1.RecordDepositResponse.title: RecordDepositResponse
banking.v1.RecordDepositResponse.description:
The chain names the owner of the deposit address the transfer landed on, so the
 credited party is always a PERSON: `party_kind` is `user` and `party_id` their banking
 id. A transfer to the treasury address is nobody's — it is refused here.

network.title: network
network.description: bep20 | polygon | trc20 | ton — the rail to ship on

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross decimal USDT to debit (the fee is taken from this)

idempotency_key.title: idempotency_key
idempotency_key.description:
Client-minted, 1..128 bytes, unique per user (the withdraw page mints one per load). A
 repeat with the same network, address and amount returns the first withdrawal and opens
 no second; the same key with other terms is ALREADY_EXISTS. Empty (a client that predates
 the field) = no deduplication.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token (proves identity).

session_id.title: session_id
session_id.description: The session id to revoke (must belong to the same user).

min_kyc_level.title: min_kyc_level
min_kyc_level.description: the concierge KYC level a user needs to move money in or pay the scope's invoices

max_moved_in_24h.title: max_moved_in_24h
max_moved_in_24h.description: rolling 24 h total moved in, per user

max_balance.title: max_balance
max_balance.description:
Ceiling on the compartment's total, applied ONLY to the user's own MoveFunds in —
 payouts, captures and refunds into the compartment are never refused for it.

caller_eligible.title: caller_eligible
caller_eligible.description:
Whether the CALLER meets `min_kyc_level` right now — the UI's reason to offer the
 move or to point at verification instead.

auto_payout_per_op.title: auto_payout_per_op
auto_payout_per_op.description:
Automatic ceilings, per (service client, scope): past them a payout or transfer
 needs an approval. Defaults 1000 / 5000 / 5000.

banking.v1.ScopePolicy.title: ScopePolicy
banking.v1.ScopePolicy.description:
What it takes to move money into a scope, and how far its services may move money
 without an approval. Limits are decimal USDT strings; an empty limit means none.

current.title: current
current.description: True for the family that owns the refresh token presented on the listing call.

banking.v1.Session.title: Session
banking.v1.Session.description: One active session = one refresh-token family. Timestamps are unix SECONDS.

banking.v1.TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
banking.v1.TokenResponse.description:
A first-party token pair plus a snapshot of the principal. All expiries are
 unix SECONDS (matching the JWT `exp` claim); the BFF parses them with
 proto-loader `longs: String`.

bank.title: bank
bank.description: mocked USD liquidity (separate ledger; off-ramp FX)

total_custody.title: total_custody
total_custody.description: sum of rail custody — the asset side

reserved_for_withdrawals.title: reserved_for_withdrawals
reserved_for_withdrawals.description: locked by in-flight withdrawals and approved payments

held_by_users.title: held_by_users
held_by_users.description: Σ user claims — what people hold directly

banking_treasury.title: banking_treasury
banking_treasury.description:
banking's own treasury, `scope_account:main:treasury` (D17): the withdrawal fees it
 retained, less what the owners approved paying out of it.

held_in_compartments.title: held_in_compartments
held_in_compartments.description: Σ users' scope compartments — still people's

banking.v1.Treasury.title: Treasury
banking.v1.Treasury.description:
The treasury picture: per-rail liquidity (Layer 2) and who the claims on it belong to
 (Layer 1). Under the unified-claim model the invariant is GLOBAL — `total_custody`
 (the asset side) equals the sum of all claims — and every claim is somebody's (#245):
 a person's (`held_by_users`, Σ `user:<id>` claims; `held_in_compartments`, Σ their scope
 compartments), or banking's own (`banking_treasury`). Nothing here
 is a remainder: each figure is read off its own accounts, and whether they add up to
 the custody is the reconciliation's finding, not this view's arithmetic.

banking.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
banking.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.description:
The caller's editable profile, full-replace. Same 10 fields as the editable part of
 UserProfile; an empty string clears the field.

in_compartments.title: in_compartments
in_compartments.description: posted across the user's scope compartments

banking.v1.UserBalanceResponse.title: UserBalanceResponse
banking.v1.UserBalanceResponse.description:
A live ledger balance for a user. `amount` and `pending` are u128 minor-unit
 decimal STRINGS (proto3 has no u128; a string is lossless and matches
 proto-loader's `longs: String`). They cover the user's whole cash — the `main` claim
 plus every scope compartment, split by `main` and `in_compartments` — and each account
 is credit-normal, so `amount` (Σ posted credits − posted debits) is non-negative by
 invariant.
 `authoritative` is true when read directly from TigerBeetle; `as_of` is unix
 seconds. The `authoritative`/`as_of` pair is the forward-compat seam for a future
 read projection — a projection may later return `authoritative=false` rows with
 no breaking proto change. (Named for the users surface; the company-money
 `BalanceService` owns its own balance messages.)

legal_name.title: legal_name
legal_name.description:
Editable profile fields (control plane; empty until the user sets them). email and
 status above stay read-only — email is the IdP's, status is admin-managed.

kyc_level.title: kyc_level
kyc_level.description:
Kept wire-identical with concierge.v1.UserProfile (the wallet TS is aliased to the
 concierge shape). The identity plane OWNS kyc/role; the money plane mirrors them for
 gating but does not re-serve them on its self-service GetMe, so these stay default
 here — the fields exist for cross-plane wire parity.

 The tier ladder, written down here because the money plane is what ENFORCES it and
 no authoritative range was stated in either plane before this:
   0 — registered. Sign-up plus a confirmed email address; nothing else is verified.
       No deposit address is issued and no withdrawal is accepted.
   1 — verified. Identity document, liveness, a face match against the document, and
       a passed sanctions/PEP screen. Deposits and withdrawals are permitted.
   2 — enhanced. Everything in 1 plus proof of address and source of funds. Carries
       raised transaction limits (the limits themselves are not modelled yet).
   3 — elevated. Enhanced due diligence; set only by a human reviewer, never
       automatically.
 Banking gates BOTH directions of money movement on >= 1. The value is set by an
 admin in the identity plane and mirrored onto the money plane by the one-way
 lifecycle bridge; banking never authors it.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from concierge's OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist
 rather than from `users.role`. Carried here only for wire parity — the money plane
 has no allowlist of its own and never sets it.

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
WHY the account is disabled, and therefore who may undo it — concierge splits the
 old blocking verb into a lapsing `admin_hold` and a ratified `governance` verdict,
 and an empty string is a THIRD case: an account suspended before the field existed,
 which keeps the one-act, never-lapsing semantics it was actually suspended under.

 Carried here only for wire parity, like `role_is_break_glass` above: the money plane
 learns of a freeze through the one-way lifecycle bridge's SUSPENDED/REINSTATED
 events, never by reading this, and never sets it. Absent them the parity round trip
 in `wallet/backend/tests/concierge_parity.rs` re-encodes short and fails, which is
 exactly the drift that test exists to catch.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses; 0 when nothing lapses. Parity only, as above.

username.title: username
username.description: Parity with concierge.v1.UserProfile.username, like the two above.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The hub's canonical user id (a UUID) — this is the JWT `sub`, never Google's sub.

role.title: role
role.description:
Kept wire-identical with concierge.v1.UserSummary (the wallet TS is aliased to the
 concierge shape). The money plane doesn't serve the role here — the wallet host reads it
 from concierge's login summary — so this stays empty; the field exists for parity.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
Parity with concierge.v1.UserSummary.role_is_break_glass — the money plane does not
 serve it, but the field number must not be reused.

banking.v1.UserSummary.title: UserSummary
banking.v1.UserSummary.description:
Minimal principal snapshot returned with a freshly issued token pair, so the BFF
 can populate a session without a second round trip.

deposit_addresses.title: deposit_addresses
deposit_addresses.description: a rail to top up on (per network)

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross debited from the user (decimal USDT)

net_amount.title: net_amount
net_amount.description: amount − fee, the amount sent on-chain

banking.v1.Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
banking.v1.Withdrawal.description:
A user withdrawal aggregate, projected. `state` advances queued → processing →
 completed (settled on confirmations) | failed (voided, refunded); a queued one may
 also be cancelled (voided, refunded).

amount.title: amount
amount.description: gross decimal USDT debited from the source

source.title: source
source.description: user | treasury — which account funds it (`treasury`: an approved payment out of banking's treasury, D17)

banking.v1.WithdrawalQueueItem.title: WithdrawalQueueItem
banking.v1.WithdrawalQueueItem.description:
One withdrawal awaiting operator action. `email` is the mirrored identity email
 (may be empty if the bridge hasn't populated it); `created_at` is unix seconds.

created_at.title: created_at
created_at.description: Unix SECONDS the user was provisioned (joined).

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role` — see UserProfile.role_is_break_glass. This is the field that
 stops the console listing an "owner" the consilium has never heard of.

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
Why the account is disabled; see UserProfile.suspended_by. On the list because a
 held account and a suspended one need different action buttons, and a console that
 cannot tell them apart offers the wrong one.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses. 0 when nothing lapses.

username.title: username
username.description: See UserProfile.username. ListUsers' query matches it as it matches the email.

concierge.v1.AdminUserSummary.title: AdminUserSummary
concierge.v1.AdminUserSummary.description:
A lightweight user row for the operator console's user list (not the full profile).
 Named distinctly from auth.proto's login `UserSummary` (same package).

delegates.title: delegates
delegates.description: Aliases of this catalog its holders may grant and revoke (GrantPermission).

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The concierge user id — the access token's `sub`.

concierge.v1.ClientTokenResponse.title: ClientTokenResponse
concierge.v1.ClientTokenResponse.description:
A relying party's token pair. Expiries are unix SECONDS. Deliberately carries no
 profile: the client reads that from `UserDirectory.GetMe` with the access token, and
 GetMe is also what it re-checks `permissions` against on every request.

code.title: code
code.description: The `code` query parameter the browser brought back to the redirect_uri.

redirect_uri.title: redirect_uri
redirect_uri.description: The redirect_uri sent to authorize, byte for byte.

code_verifier.title: code_verifier
code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 challenge was sent to authorize.

username.title: username
username.description: The holder's handle; empty when they have none. A delegate sees it as it sees the email.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Recorded on the grant and the audit row.

account.title: account
account.description: An email or a username: one handle, resolved the way a password sign-in resolves it.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
REQUIRED. A brake that stops someone's money with no stated cause cannot be
 reviewed afterwards, and the owners asked to ratify it are reading exactly this.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS the hold lapses unless the owners ratify it.

concierge.v1.Jwk.title: Jwk
concierge.v1.Jwk.description:
One JSON Web Key. Ed25519 keys are OKP: kty="OKP", crv="Ed25519", x=base64url
 public key, alg="EdDSA". `kid` is a stable thumbprint of the public key.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token: proves identity and flags the current session.

query.title: query
query.description: Free-text match over email/user_id (empty = no text filter).

limit.title: limit
limit.description: Page window. `limit` is clamped server-side; `offset` is a simple row offset.

total.title: total
total.description: Total matching the filters (before the page window), for the list header count.

revoke_all.title: revoke_all
revoke_all.description:
When true, bump the user's token_version (coarse "revoke all"), not just this
 refresh family.

orphaned.title: orphaned
orphaned.description: The tenant's current catalog defines nothing this target names: it grants nothing.

concierge.v1.PermissionGrant.title: PermissionGrant
concierge.v1.PermissionGrant.description: One grant of a target inside a tenant's namespace.

version.title: version
version.description:
Unix SECONDS of the commit the client was built from (nix `self.lastModified`):
 build time, not boot time, so a restarting older replica never supersedes a newer one.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Recorded verbatim on the audit row.

account.title: account
account.description: An email or a username, as in GrantPermissionRequest.

refresh_token.title: refresh_token
refresh_token.description: The caller's current refresh token (proves identity).

session_id.title: session_id
session_id.description: The session id to revoke (must belong to the same user).

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
Recorded verbatim on the audit row. Optional here: revoking sessions is the
 reflex you want an operator to reach for without composing a sentence first.

current.title: current
current.description: True for the family that owns the refresh token presented on the listing call.

concierge.v1.Session.title: Session
concierge.v1.Session.description: One active session = one refresh-token family. Timestamps are unix SECONDS.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Recorded verbatim on the audit row.

kyc_level.title: kyc_level
kyc_level.description: The user's KYC level now in effect (echoes the applied level).

role.title: role
role.description:
The role to grant (snake_case: investor/operator/admin/owner).

 `owner` is refused in both directions and `admin` in the GRANTING direction, each
 naming the proposal that does it instead. Taking `admin` away is still one act:
 containing a rogue operator must never be the slower path.

reason.title: reason
reason.description: Recorded verbatim on the audit row.

role.title: role
role.description: The role now in effect (echoes the applied role).

concierge.v1.TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
concierge.v1.TokenResponse.description:
A first-party token pair plus a snapshot of the principal. All expiries are
 unix SECONDS (matching the JWT `exp` claim); the BFF parses them with
 proto-loader `longs: String`.

concierge.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
concierge.v1.UpdateProfileRequest.description:
The caller's editable profile, full-replace. Same 10 fields as the editable part of
 UserProfile; an empty string clears the field.

legal_name.title: legal_name
legal_name.description:
Editable profile fields (control plane; empty until the user sets them). email and
 status above stay read-only — email is the IdP's, status is admin-managed.

kyc_level.title: kyc_level
kyc_level.description: The user's KYC level (admin-managed; mirrored to the money plane).

role.title: role
role.description:
The user's platform access role (snake_case: investor/operator/admin/owner).
 Admin-managed via SetRole; read-only here.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role`. See UserSummary.role_is_break_glass in auth.proto — same flag,
 same meaning: real authority, granted by the environment while the fund has no
 persisted owner, seating nobody. Render it as a warning, never as ownership.

suspended_by.title: suspended_by
suspended_by.description:
WHY the account is disabled — and therefore who may undo it. Empty on an active
 user, and also on one suspended before this field existed (those keep the old
 one-act, never-lapsing semantics they were actually suspended under).
   "admin_hold"  — one operator's brake; lapses at hold_expires_at; ReinstateUser
                   lifts it in one act.
   "governance"  — the owners' ratified verdict; never lapses; ReinstateUser
                   refuses and names ProposeUserReinstatement.

hold_expires_at.title: hold_expires_at
hold_expires_at.description: Unix SECONDS an "admin_hold" lapses. 0 when nothing lapses.

permissions.title: permissions
permissions.description:
What the caller may do, concrete: no alias, no wildcard. Filled by GetMe only. To a
 relying party, its tenant's namespace and nothing else; to a first-party session, the
 seat's permissions plus every tenant's. A relying party gates on this alone.

username.title: username
username.description:
A handle beside the email, interchangeable with it wherever an account is named.
 Empty when the account has none.

user_id.title: user_id
user_id.description: The concierge canonical user id (a UUID) — this is the JWT `sub`, never Google's sub.

role.title: role
role.description:
The user's platform access role (snake_case: investor/operator/admin/owner), so the
 BFF can gate the admin console at sign-in without a second round trip. Read-only.

role_is_break_glass.title: role_is_break_glass
role_is_break_glass.description:
True when `role` above came from the OWNER_SUBJECTS emergency allowlist rather than
 from `users.role`. It is real authority, but it is the environment's and not the
 register's: it disappears the moment the fund has its first persisted owner, and it
 seats nobody. A client MUST render it as a warning, never as ownership.

username.title: username
username.description: Empty when the account has no handle.

concierge.v1.UserSummary.title: UserSummary
concierge.v1.UserSummary.description:
Minimal principal snapshot returned with a freshly issued token pair, so the BFF
 can populate a session without a second round trip.

connect-protocol-version.title: Connect-Protocol-Version
connect-protocol-version.description: Define the version of the Connect protocol

code.description: The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].

message.description: A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.

details.description: A list of messages that carry the error details. There is no limit on the number of messages.

type.description: A URL that acts as a globally unique identifier for the type of the serialized message. For example: `type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo`. This is used to determine the schema of the data in the `value` field and is the discriminator for the `debug` field.

value.description: The Protobuf message, serialized as bytes and base64-encoded. The specific message type is identified by the `type` field.

debug.title: Debug
debug.description: Deserialized error detail payload. The 'type' field indicates the schema. This field is for easier debugging and should not be relied upon for application logic.

connect.error_details.Any.description: Contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a @type that describes the type of the serialized message, with an additional debug field for ConnectRPC error details.

tags.name: banking.v1.AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService — the money plane's token issuance and authorization surface.

 This is the MONEY plane: it does NOT do third-party (Google) OAuth — identity and
 sign-in live wholly in the concierge plane. Users are mirrored here by the one-way
 cross-plane bridge (concierge `CREATED` → a local row keyed by `auth_subject`).
 This service only issues/rotates the hub's OWN first-party asymmetric JWTs
 (EdDSA/Ed25519, `aud=banking-core`) for those already-identified users, and
 publishes verification keys. Services do NOT call this per request to authorize:
 they verify access tokens locally against the cached JWKS via the shared
 `evbanking_auth` flow (no round trip, no per-service token storage). They DO call
 `Jwks` periodically to refresh that cache, since the hub speaks only gRPC (no HTTP
 `.well-known` endpoint).

 `IssueUserToken` is the concierge→banking token-exchange seam: after the wallet host
 BFF authenticates a user against concierge, it calls this server-to-server (with the
 shared bridge issuance token, NOT a user token) to mint the money-plane pair for that
 user. Banking trusts its OWN service credential, never concierge's issuer — so a
 leaked concierge token can't move money. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.BalanceService
tags.description:
BalanceService — the bank's treasury and the money plane's operator surface.

 Reads authoritative balances from the TigerBeetle ledger; metadata and events from
 Postgres. Every amount is a decimal USDT STRING (proto3 has no u128; a string is
 lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`). All RPCs are admin-gated
 (allowlist) at the boundary. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

 banking's own money is its treasury, `scope_account:main:treasury` (D17): the withdrawal fees it keeps, which
 nothing pays out until concierge's scope approvals decide its spending
 (`bank:treasury_surplus`, D24).

tags.name: banking.v1.HealthService
tags.description:
Health surface for the hub's gRPC service plane.

   Check     — liveness: is the process up? Trivial, unauthenticated; backs the
               wallet BFF smoke path (browser -> BFF -> gRPC) and service checks.
   Readiness — can this instance actually move money? Pings Postgres + TigerBeetle
               and inspects the outbox (parked rows / dispatch backlog). An
               orchestrator/LB drains an instance that is up but not ready instead of
               routing money-moving traffic to it.

tags.name: banking.v1.WalletService
tags.description:
WalletService — a user's own crypto wallet: one unified USDT balance, deposit
 addresses, and withdrawals. Networks (BEP20/Polygon/TRC20/TON) are a transaction attribute
 (where you deposit / where a withdrawal ships), never a balance dimension — the user
 holds a single fungible USDT balance, segmented by lifecycle.

 Every RPC acts on the caller's own access-token `sub`. Balances are read live from the
 authoritative TigerBeetle ledger (Read-First); amounts are decimal USDT STRINGS
 (proto3 has no u128; a string is lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`).
 A withdrawal is a queued saga (reserve → dispatch → settle/void): it is accepted even
 when the chosen rail is short on liquidity and queued until the treasury tops it up.
 The operator-driven dispatch/settle/fail RPCs live on BalanceService; the custody
 broadcast and deposit-address derivation sit behind ports (a stub in this scaffold).
 See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.CompartmentService
tags.description:
CompartmentService — the caller's wallet split by scope (`main`, `invest`, `sa`, …),
 as on an exchange with sub-accounts: `main` is the wallet above (deposits arrive
 there, withdrawals leave from there); every other scope the user has entered holds
 a compartment, money earmarked for that scope's services. Only the user moves money
 between `main` and a compartment — instantly and without a fee — and never between
 two non-main scopes directly. A user is identified by their `auth_subject`.

 A separate service, not new fields on `Wallet`: WalletService keeps its shape while
 the compartments are built behind it, and its `Balance` carries only their sum
 (`in_compartments`). Every RPC acts on the caller's own `sub`.

 FIRST-PARTY ONLY. Every MUTATING wallet route — `WalletService.RequestWithdrawal`,
 `WalletService.CancelWithdrawal`, `MoveFunds`, `GrantMandate`, `RevokeMandate`, and
 `InvoicePaymentService.PayInvoice` — is accepted only from
 `Origin: https://evinvest.ltd`. A scope's host may read balances and history
 cross-origin; to act it opens the wallet page on evinvest.ltd and learns the result
 by `postMessage` with the origin checked. The CSRF token is never in a body a
 cross-origin read can see.

 FROZEN. A frozen user's new debits — MoveFunds into a scope, PayInvoice — are
 FAILED_PRECONDITION `user_frozen`; a FROZEN scope takes no MoveFunds in
 (`scope_frozen`), a CLOSED one neither (`scope_closed`). Credits, reads and MoveFunds
 back to `main` go on: that money never leaves the platform, so neither a freeze nor the
 outflow pause stops it.

tags.name: banking.v1.InvoicePaymentService
tags.description:
InvoicePaymentService — the payer's side of an invoice a scope issued
 (`scope.v1.InvoiceService`). The user opens it from the scope's link in the wallet
 page or the `<ev-pay-invoice>` element and pays it straight into the scope's
 account from `main` or from their compartment in that scope — no move between
 compartments first. Every RPC acts on the caller's own `sub`.

 Paying is first-party: `PayInvoice` is accepted only from
 `Origin: https://evinvest.ltd` (see `CompartmentService`), and an invoice's
 `pay_url` always points there. Whichever source pays, the RECEIVING scope's
 `min_kyc_level` applies to the payer (FAILED_PRECONDITION `kyc_level`); a frozen
 payer is `user_frozen`.

tags.name: banking.v1.OperationsService
tags.description:
OperationsService — the caller's activity timeline: every money event that touched
 their account, in one time-ordered stream.

 A pure CQRS **read model**. Deposits and withdrawals are separate records, each with
 its own list; what neither can answer is "what happened, in order". This service is
 that join, done once in the hub over the Postgres projections.

 Read-only: it moves no money and owns no state. Every RPC acts on the caller's own
 access-token `sub`. Amounts are decimal USDT STRINGS (proto3 has no u128; a string is
 lossless and matches proto-loader's `longs: String`).
 See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and piggybank/core/PATTERNS.md.

tags.name: banking.v1.PaymentsService
tags.description:
PaymentsService — the ORDER that moves money between two named ends of the platform.

 Two tiers on one order, DERIVED from the destination and never supplied: an external
 wallet address (L1, settled by the withdrawal saga), an internal claim (L3, one posted
 transfer). See domain/src/payments.rs for the aggregate.

 AUTHORIZATION IS A FUNCTION OF THE SOURCE. A payment out of an investor's own claim
 (`user:<id>`) is answered by THAT investor, signed in, over PaymentConfirmationService.
 A payment out of banking's treasury (`treasury`, D17) needs the owners' approval at every
 tier: a concierge approval of kind `bank:payment`, proposed in the initiator's name, which
 needs their access token of the last two minutes in `x-ev-user-token`. There is
 deliberately no cell in which one admin moves the treasury alone. The treasury is never
 a destination; as a source it is CLOSED until its spending is decided by concierge's
 scope approvals (`bank:treasury_surplus`, D24) — OpenPayment out of it is
 FAILED_PRECONDITION `treasury spending waits for scope approvals`.

 IMMUTABILITY. There is no edit RPC. `payload_hash` binds the approval to the exact terms
 shown to the approver; changing anything means cancel and reopen.

tags.name: banking.v1.PaymentConfirmationService
tags.description:
PaymentConfirmationService — the investor's side of a payment out of THEIR claim, signed in.
 Behind the user-auth layer: the caller is the subject, and an order that is not theirs, has
 no such seat or does not exist is the same NOT_FOUND. The session is the credential,
 and the wallet host's gate asks for a fresh login before an approval (a decline asks for none).

tags.name: banking.v1.PayoutReviewService
tags.description:
PayoutReviewService — the lines of a `bank:scope_payout` operation, for the people who
 are asked to approve it (banking#529, SCOPE-LEDGER checklist item 9).

 The approval concierge shows carries only totals, the largest single line and two flags;
 the approvers could not see WHO is paid HOW MUCH. This is the read behind the page that
 shows them. It reads the operation banking STORED when the payout was requested — the same
 rows the approval's `lines_digest` was taken over and the executor pays from — never
 anything a caller sends.

 Read-only: it moves no money and writes nothing. Who may read is decided at the wallet host's
 BFF, which has the caller's concierge session: only a voter on the approval's frozen roster
 gets a page. This service refuses what it can check itself — an unknown operation, one that
 is not a payout, one whose approval is not opened, and a caller-supplied `approval_id` that
 is not the operation's own — all with one identical NOT_FOUND, so a probe learns nothing
 about which ids exist. Amounts are canonical decimal USDT strings.

tags.name: banking.v1.UsersService
tags.description:
UsersService — investor accounts and their investments.

 Identity metadata is the Postgres control plane; money is read live from the
 authoritative TigerBeetle ledger and is NEVER re-bookkept in Postgres. Every
 RPC is authorized from the verified access-token Claims injected by core's
 inbound auth layer; self-service RPCs act on the caller's own `sub`, admin RPCs
 are gated by the hub's admin allowlist (config). See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

tags.name: concierge.v1.UserDirectory
tags.description:
UserDirectory — the authoritative user/identity control plane.

 Owns investor accounts and their profile metadata. This is the identity plane:
 money lives in the separate banking plane and is NEVER mirrored here. Every RPC
 is authorized from the verified access-token Claims injected by the inbound auth
 layer; self-service RPCs act on the caller's own `sub`, admin RPCs are gated by
 the admin allowlist (config).

tags.name: concierge.v1.AuthService
tags.description:
AuthService — the concierge plane's token issuance and authorization surface.

 Issues first-party asymmetric JWTs (EdDSA/Ed25519), rotates refresh tokens, and
 publishes verification keys. Services do NOT call this per request to authorize:
 they verify access tokens locally against the cached JWKS via the shared
 `evconcierge_auth` flow (no round trip, no per-service token storage). They DO call
 `Jwks` periodically to refresh that cache, since concierge speaks only gRPC (no HTTP
 `.well-known` endpoint).

 Sign-in itself (Google, GitHub, emailed code, password) is the plane's own HTTP
 surface (`/auth/*`, reached as `evinvest.ltd/api/auth/*`), which opens the session
 in process; no RPC signs anybody in.
